leftEvidence.title: Peter carries Noah’s water into a difficult baptism argument

points.label: Noah-relative action
points.left: Christ’s suffering, death, life in the Spirit, proclamation to imprisoned spirits, divine patience, Noah’s ship, eight people, and water appear in one compressed sequence.
points.right: Noah and seven others are preserved while the ancient world is judged; the passage also remembers angels, Sodom, Gomorrah, and Lot.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Baptism is called a corresponding figure and is distinguished from bodily dirt removal through conscience, resurrection, and Christ’s exaltation.
points.right: These examples support the claim that the Lord knows how to deliver the godly and reserve the unrighteous for judgment.

payload.posture: 1 Peter places Noah inside a Christ, spirits, water, and baptism sequence; 2 Peter places him inside examples of judgment and deliverance.

rightEvidence.title: Peter calls Noah a preacher of righteousness

payload.tension: The shared Noah memory supports different arguments and should not be forced into one explanation.
payload.title: Two apostolic uses of Noah
